## 1 — DELIVERABLE 1: THE DEGREE SPLIT. It settles.

### 1a — the arm × input matrix

`.temp/t136/k29.c` is `TASK_133`'s `k29_bst.c` — same tree, same fold, same
driver, same op encoding — with six arms behind `-DHARDEN`. The only additions
are the saved binding's bookkeeping (`g_key`, `g_fresh`), **present in every arm
including R1**, exactly as `p27`'s `c/kernel.c` carries `live[]`, so that H3
differs from R1 by one conjunct and nothing else.

```
-DHARDEN=0  R1.  `if (saved)`                                        THE BUG
-DHARDEN=1  write path, at every free():   if (t == g_saved) g_saved = NULL;
-DHARDEN=2  write path, at the located VICTIM, ONE site:  the same line
-DHARDEN=3  read path, ONE CONJUNCT:  && g_fresh
-DHARDEN=4  read path, ONE CONJUNCT:  && g_saved->key == g_key
-DHARDEN=5  read path, ONE CONJUNCT:  && g_saved == nfind(root, g_key)
```

### 1c — ⚠⚠ WHY `TASK_133`'s CANDIDATE FAILED: the SITE, not the mechanism

`TASK_133` §7 put the one-line family down as *"(b) null-the-cache, which is one
conjunct and **does not fix the recycle half**"*. That is true of **where it put
the line** and false of the line.

`nrem`'s two-child case does not free the victim — but it *does* delete the
successor, **by calling `nrem` again**. So the site *"at the located victim,
`if (k == t->key)`"* is reached **twice**: once for the victim (whose contents
are about to be overwritten) and once for the successor (which is about to be
freed). One site, both events, and it is exact by induction over `nrem` — which
is what the 1500-window fuzz then confirms at `0/1500`.

⚠ **H1 and H2 have DISJOINT blind spots and that is the proof the placement is
the whole story**: on `i06 SUCCESSOR` (FIND the successor, then remove a
two-child ancestor) H1 catches it and H2 catches it; on the two-child victims H1
misses and H2 catches. The mechanism — *"null the cached pointer"* — never
changed.

### 1d — ⚠⚠ THE READ-PATH ANALOGUE OF `live[h] == 1` CANNOT BE RUN, BECAUSE RUNNING IT IS THE BUG

The task file asks what `p29`'s analogue of `p27`'s **read-path** conjunct is.
Measured answer: **there is no read-path conjunct that is both exact and safe.**

`H4` is the exact predicate spelled directly — `&& g_saved->key == g_key`, i.e.
literally *"does the node still hold the value `saved` was taken from"*. It is
**correct on the two-child inputs and is itself a heap-use-after-free on the
leaf inputs** (5 of 11 abort under ASan). The check that would answer the
question dereferences the pointer whose validity is the question.

> ⚠⚠ **So `p29`'s safety line is on the WRITE path and `p27`'s is on the READ path, and that is a mechanism difference, not a spelling one.** `p27`'s bug is *the read does not ask*; `p29`'s is *the mutation does not tell*. Two temporal rows, opposite halves of one obligation.

That is a *necessary* condition for "one conjunct" and a generous one: it
accepts the conjunct anywhere in the condition. **The script reproduces the hand

| form of the added safety line | n | patterns |
|---|---|---|
| **a conjunct on an existing test** | **4** | `p17` `p22` `p23` `p27` |
| a new `if` statement / guard wrapper / early return | 13 | `p02` `p03` `p04` `p05` `p06` `p07` `p09` `p12` `p14` `p16` `p18` `p36` `p46` |

**4 of 25 = 16%.** The invariant that actually holds across all 25 is ***one

### 2a — ✅ the bug survives the PINNED kernel shape

`TASK_133` proved expressibility with `Node *l, *r`. That shape has no R5:
Verus needs a permission per allocation, and `p27` gets that from a **flat slot
table** with a `Map<usize, PointsTo>` keyed by slot. `.temp/t136/p29c/kernel.c`
is `p29` rebuilt on `p27`'s machinery — records still individually `malloc`'d
(so the free is a real free and the bug stays temporal, not `p17`'s logical
class), tree links are **slot ids inside the record**, and the only pointer the
kernel holds is `g_saved`, the one a `FIND` op saves.

`.temp/t136/logs/d2-pinned-shape.log`, against an independent model
(`.temp/t136/p29c/model.py`):

```
      input |          model |             R1                R1 ASan |     R1h 1-site          @free
   v10 deg2 | 69224958592225 |     4958448385                      - |             OK     4958448385
   v5  deg0 | 69224958592225 |     ASan-abort    heap-use-after-free |             OK             OK
   v20 deg2 | 69224958592225 |     4958517825                      - |             OK     4958517825
   v15 deg0 | 69224958592225 |     ASan-abort    heap-use-after-free |             OK             OK
   v25 deg0 | 69224958592225 |     ASan-abort    heap-use-after-free |             OK             OK
  successor | 69224958592225 |     ASan-abort    heap-use-after-free |             OK             OK
    recycle | 69224958446154 |     ASan-abort    heap-use-after-free |             OK             OK
  unrelated | 69224958517825 |             OK                      - |             OK             OK
     benign |  8684676248263 |             OK                      - |             OK             OK

fuzz, 1200 windows:  R1h ONE-SITE != model : 0      R1h @free != model : 26
                     R1 harm: ASan-abort 114, SILENTLY WRONG 26, right 1060
ASan POSITIVE CONTROL: rc=1 hits=2 heap-use-after-free
```

✅ **Both bug classes survive, the one-site line is still exact (`0/1200`), and
`TASK_133`'s placement still misses exactly the ASan-silent set.**

⚠ **Disclosure — I broke this myself first and my own model hid it.** My first
deletion loop re-searched *by key* after the substitution, which finds the
victim again (it now holds the successor's key) and spins to the guard; the
Python model mirrored the same algorithm, so the two agreed and the table looked
clean. It was caught by the one input designed to be different (`successor`
reading `OK` when it must abort). **A model that mirrors the implementation
agrees by construction — `check.py`'s own model-sandbox rule, met in the wild.**
Fixed by moving the *cursor* to the successor instead of re-searching; both
sides rewritten; the fuzz is what re-decides it.

### 2c — ⚠⚠⚠ THE R5 ARMS. The linear resource is blind to the same half.

`.memory/02-bench-rules.md`: *"Every temporal R5 owes an ATTACK arm that must
FAIL to verify."* `.temp/t136/verus/p29_r5_probe.rs` carries four, on `p27`'s
`rec_alloc`/`rec_free`/`rec_open`/`rec_close`/`rec_read` **verbatim**, one arm
per `--cfg`. `.temp/t136/logs/d2-verus-arms.log`:

```
===== ARM_A =====   control: alloc, write 7, read.        ensures r == 7
verification results:: 6 verified, 0 errors                          <- MUST VERIFY. does.

===== ARM_B =====   USE AFTER FREE: rec_close, then read the saved pointer
error: precondition not satisfied      (perms.tracked_borrow(0))
error: precondition not satisfied      (rec_read: pt.ptr() == p)
verification results:: 5 verified, 1 errors                          <- MUST FAIL. does.

===== ARM_C =====   USE AFTER RECYCLE: the splice overwrites in place, nothing
                    is freed, the SAVED pointer is read.   ensures r == 9
verification results:: 6 verified, 0 errors                          <- ⚠⚠⚠ VERIFIES

===== ARM_D =====   the SAME program with the functional postcondition the row
                    is about: "the USE returns what the FIND found". ensures r == 7
error: postcondition not satisfied
verification results:: 5 verified, 1 errors
```

⚠ **ARM_C's `ensures` is `r == 9`, not a tautology.** It does not merely fail to
complain — it **proves the stale read returns the recycled occupant's value**,
`6 verified, 0 errors`, while holding the permission. If the linear resource saw
this bug that could not verify.

> ### ⚠⚠⚠ THE TRANSFERABLE SENTENCE
>
> **`p27`'s temporal mechanism tracks the ALLOCATION, not the BINDING.**
> `deallocate` consumes the `PointsTo`, so *use-after-free* is unprovable —
> ARM_B. The splice deallocates nothing, so *use-after-recycle* is not merely
> provable, it is **proved** — ARM_C. What rejects it is the **functional**
> postcondition, ARM_D, and nothing about linearity.
>
> ⚠ **This scopes RECAP finding 47.** *"VERUS CAN STATE 'NO USE-AFTER-FREE' — a
> linear `PointsTo`, proven, zero extra TCB … **LINEARITY IS THE LINE**"* is
> true as written and is narrower than it reads: what linearity states is
> *"no use after DEALLOCATION"*. It cannot state *"no use after the OCCUPANT
> CHANGED"*. **`p42`'s failure mode is available here in an R5 that looks
> completely healthy** — and that is precisely the case the attack-arm rule
> exists for.

✅ **And it lines up with §2b, with ASan, and with §2f.** **FOUR** independent
mechanisms split on **one** fault line, because all four are mechanisms about
the ALLOCATION and `p29`'s second class never touches it:

| mechanism | use-after-FREE (leaf victim) | use-after-RECYCLE (two-child victim) |
|---|---|---|
| ASan | `heap-use-after-free`, aborts | **silent** |
| safe Rust `Option<Box<Rec>>` | correct, 71/71 | **wrong, bit-identical to buggy C, 17/17** |
| Verus linear `PointsTo` | unprovable (ARM_B) | **verifies `6/0`, and PROVES the recycled value** (ARM_C) |
| R1's own checksum | **non-reproducible** (19–20 distinct in 20 runs, and the count moves too) | reproducible, 1 of 20 |

⚠ **The fourth row inverts the convenience of the other three**: the half every
detector sees is the half that cannot be gated, and the half nothing sees is the
half that reproduces.

### 2d — ✅ RECONCILING §2b WITH `TASK_133` §3c: it is slot recycling, measured

Hypothesis: the disagreement is one design decision, not the language. Test:
**the same safe source, four builds** (`--cfg recycle` puts freed slots on a
free list and reuses them; `ntab` stays the high-water mark and the capacity
guard is unchanged, so the *abstract* semantics is identical and only *which
slot* a record occupies moves). `.temp/t136/logs/d2-recycle-reconcile.log`:

```
      input |     no recycle, naive   no recycle, +1 line        RECYCLE, naive      RECYCLE, +1 line
   v10 deg2 |        69224958448385                    OK        69224958448385                    OK
   v5  deg0 |                    OK                    OK                    OK                    OK
    recycle |                    OK                    OK        69224958444015                    OK
     benign |                    OK                    OK                    OK                    OK
        ... (full table in the log)

FUZZ, 700 windows -- wrong-answer counts:
         no recycle, naive : 17
       no recycle, +1 line : 0
            RECYCLE, naive : 36
          RECYCLE, +1 line : 0
```

✅ **Confirmed.** With recycling the naive safe rung is wrong **36** times
instead of 17 — the extra 19 are leaf victims whose freed slot a later insert
takes back, so the read returns the *new occupant*. On the `recycle` hand input
it is `69224958444015`, **bit-identical to buggy C's plain-build answer**. That
is `TASK_133`'s index arena, and both results are true of their own program.

> ⚠⚠ **SO THE SHIPPED `p29` HAS TO PICK, AND THE PICK CHANGES THE HEADLINE:**
> **no-recycle** (`p27`'s convention — `ntab` only grows, which is what keeps
> `live[]` a one-bit generation counter and R5's permission map tractable) →
> *safe Rust fails on exactly the half ASan cannot see*. **Recycle** → *safe
> Rust fails on both halves*.
> **My recommendation is NO-RECYCLE**, on three grounds: it is `p27`'s shipped
> convention and therefore not a choice made for this row; it is what makes R5
> tractable; and it is the **less flattering** option for the row's headline —
> it makes safe Rust look *better*, not worse.

### 2e — what remains, and the one item that dominates it

Settled and written down, so the next task does not re-derive it:

| decision | answer | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R1h's safety line | `if (tab[cur] == g_saved) g_saved = NULL;`, ONE site, at the top of the deletion loop | §1a–1c, §2a |
| the spec | `SPEC_EXACT` — the USE contributes the saved record's `val` iff that record is still in the tree and still holds the key it was found under | `.temp/t136/p29c/model.py` |
| the kernel shape | `p27`'s slot table, `CAP=32`, `RECSZ=4` (`key,val,left,right`), `NIL=255`, `SENT=251`, slots **never recycled** | §2a, §2d |
| R2/R3's representation | `Option<Box<Rec>>` + a saved **slot index** (safe Rust cannot hold the pointer — `E0502`, and that is generic borrowck, **not** this row's mechanism) | §2b, `TASK_133` §3d |
| R4/R5 | `p27`'s `Map<usize, PointsTo>` keyed by slot; the proof never has to know it is a BST | §2c |
| the R5 attack arm | ARM_D, and it must fail for the **functional** reason | §2c |

⚠ **THE ONE ITEM THAT DOMINATES THE REST, and it is why this is not a one-task
build: all 26 shipped contracts pin `ensures result == <name>_fold(buf, off,
len)` — 26 of 26, verified by parsing every `slb-contract` fence.** So `p29`'s
R5 owes a **full functional refinement** of a raw-pointer slot table against an
abstract machine with three walks (insert, find, and a two-phase delete with a
successor descent), where `p27`'s is a flat table with none. Two consequences
the next task should not discover late:

- every walk needs an explicit step bound (`while cur != NIL && steps < CAP`) in
  **every** rung, because the abstract machine over arbitrary link bytes can
  cycle and `decreases` needs a measure the tree invariant would otherwise have
  to supply;
- `p27`'s `verus.rs` is 919 lines and its `spec.md` 703, including a
  named-spelling paragraph that must appear **verbatim** (`check.py` stage 0,
  `named_spelling_problem`).

### 2f — ⚠⚠⚠ IS R1's CHECKSUM REPRODUCIBLE? `p25`'s KILL, ASKED OF `p29`

RECAP finding 48 kills `p25` three ways, and kill (3) is *"R1 has no
reproducible checksum — same binary, same input, `3196606969367904911` then
`4868875711876342483` — **and a nondeterministic R1 cannot be gated against
`model.py` at all**"*. ⚠ **A refusal's reason is what gets reused on the next
row, and `p29`'s R1 reads freed memory, so this had to be asked.** I nearly
missed it: I noticed R1's plain-build value moving between my own runs.

`.temp/t136/p29c/repro.py`, same binary, same input, 20 runs, **plain build**
(the gate's checksum cells are plain — ASan appears only at stage 7).
`.temp/t136/logs/d2-reproducibility.log`:

```
             input |  R1 distinct values |  R1h distinct values
    v5   deg0  UAF |                  19 |                    1
    v25  deg0  UAF |                  20 |                    1        <- was 18 on the previous run
  v10  deg2  RECYC |                   1 |                    1
  v20  deg2  RECYC |                   1 |                    1
            benign |                   1 |                    1
```

⚠⚠ **THE `20` WAS `18` ON THE PREVIOUS RUN AND I AM NOT QUOTING EITHER AS A
FACT.** The distinct-count of a nondeterministic value is itself
nondeterministic — **`p23`'s exact lesson, reproduced here before the row was
built rather than after four gate runs**: *"the distinct-checksum count is not a
fact and cannot be made one"*. The invariant is what stands: **the UAF inputs
are non-reproducible and the recycle inputs are stable at 1**, and `p29`'s
`NOTES.md` must publish that sentence and no number.

> ⚠⚠⚠ **THE KILL APPLIES TO HALF THE INPUTS AND NOT TO THE ROW.** Reading a
> **freed** block is nondeterministic — 19 of 20 runs distinct. Reading a
> **recycled** block is not: the read is in bounds of a live allocation whose
> contents the program itself determined, so it is stable at `1 of 20`. Benign
> is stable, and **R1h is stable everywhere**.

**Consequences for the build, and they are cheap:**

- **benign inputs** are deterministic in every rung, so gate stage 2
  (*every cell prints `model.py`'s checksum*) is unaffected;
- **adversarial RECYCLE inputs** are deterministic and R1 diverges by a
  **stable** value — a real, quotable harm row;
- **adversarial UAF inputs** must be declared non-reproducible and **no number
  may be pinned on them**. `p23`'s precedent is exact — four gate runs gave
  `7, 7, 8, 8` and the resolution was *"`NOTES.md` publishes the INVARIANT and
  no number"*. Their instrument is stage 7's `sanitizer_expect: fires`, not the
  checksum.

✅ **So `p25`'s reason does NOT transfer wholesale, and applying it to `p29` by
name would have refused a buildable row.** That is the failure mode RECAP warns
about in the same breath as the kill.

## 3 — WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHAT I AM UNSURE OF

- **No pattern was built.** `harness/check.py p29` was never run because there is
  no `p29`. `check.py` and `measure.py` were not invoked at all; **no gate or
  measurement record was touched.**
- **No cost axis was measured, deliberately.** The task file forbids
  manufacturing a performance headline and `p29`'s property is limb 4 clause 3.
  I publish **no rung-to-rung difference**, so the count-the-levers rule has
  nothing to bite on. ⚠ For the record, the one number a reader might want —
  what the safety line costs — is **not** in this report, and quoting it would
  need both rungs' spellings searched. Neither side was searched.
- **The correctness differences I DO publish are spelling-sensitive, and I
  searched two spellings on the safe side and reconciled them** (§2d). I searched
  **one** spelling on the C side (`p27`'s slot table) and **one** on the Verus
  side. A different C shape could move §2a; a different permission encoding
  could in principle move §2c, though I do not see how.
- **`H3` (`&& g_fresh`) is a live alternative I did not pursue.** It is the only
  candidate that is a *read-path conjunct*, i.e. the closest structural analogue
  of `p27`. It is **conservative** — `SPEC_FRESH ≠ SPEC_EXACT` on 270/1500
  windows — and it constrains the benign inputs (no `REMOVE` may fall between a
  `FIND` and its `USE`, or R1 and R1h disagree on a *benign* input and gate
  stage 2 fails). I recommend `H2`; I am **not certain** that is right, and it
  is the call I would most like attacked.
- **`p29`'s admissibility rests on my §2b/§2c reading**, not on a reviewed one.
  A reader who counts bug classes will still see `p27 ∪ p04` — `TASK_133` §9
  flagged exactly this and I have not removed the objection, I have sharpened
  what is new: *the three mechanisms fail together, and the failure is
  structural*.
- **Miri was not run** on the safe rung. `TASK_133` ran it on its own shape
  (clean, positive control firing); I did not re-run it on the pinned shape and
  the pinned shape is not the one it cleared.
- **`ARM_B`'s first spelling was a Rust `E0382`, not a verification failure**, and
  I rewrote it through a permission `Map` so that it fails *the way the kernel
  would*. The `E0382` version is arguably the stronger result (the attack cannot
  be *written*), but it is not what the gate would exercise.

## 4 — CLEAN NEGATIVES: named attacks that did not land

1. **"`H2` is exact only on the hand inputs."** No — `0/1500` on the original
   shape and `0/1200` on the pinned shape, two independent models.
2. **"The one-site line only works because `nrem` is recursive."** No. The
   pinned kernel's delete is an **iterative** loop and the site is still single,
   because the cursor moves to the successor rather than the key being
   re-searched. (⚠ Re-searching by key is what I got wrong first; it finds the
   victim again. §2a.)
3. **"Safe Rust's advantage in §2b is an artefact of `-O`."** Not tested at other
   levels — recorded as untested rather than claimed.
4. **"The two specs differ only on contrived inputs."** No — `SPEC_FRESH` vs
   `SPEC_EXACT` split on **270 of 1500** ordinary random windows, 18%.
5. **"ASan is simply blind on this box."** Positive control fires in every probe
   (`rc=1`, `hits=2`, `heap-use-after-free`), and the same binaries report clean
   on the benign inputs.
